questions.title: Share of bachelor’s degrees earned by women in the United States
questions.unitLabel: % of bachelor’s degrees awarded to women
questions.hint: Think about when careers in law, medicine and business opened up to women, and what that meant for college.
questions.explanation: It barely moved: 49.0% in 1980 and 58.5% in 2022. Each year is the academic year ending then. From 1996 NCES counts degree-granting colleges, a slightly different set than before.

source.attribution: US National Center for Education Statistics

questions.title: Share of electricity from wind and solar in Germany
questions.hint: Wind and solar both started from almost nothing, and both have gotten much cheaper.
questions.explanation: It rose to 42% in 2024, from 8% in 2010.

questions.title: Deaths in drink-driving crashes in Great Britain
questions.hint: Breathalysers, hard-hitting Christmas TV campaigns, drinking moving from pubs to homes, safer cars, and a legal alcohol limit that England never lowered.
questions.explanation: It fell to 220 in 2024, from 1,170 in 1984. Campaigns, enforcement and changing attitudes cut deaths to 540 by 1993, but progress then stalled for over a decade (580 in 2004). A second drop to 240 in 2010 was followed by another long plateau. An estimate from police reports and coroners’ blood tests.

questions.title: Divorce rate in Japan
questions.hint: Old village customs, a new family law after 1945, women’s growing independence, a long recession, then fewer and later marriages.
questions.explanation: It went from 0.74 in 1960 to a high of 2.10 in 2000, then ended at 1.57 in 2020. Divorce was common in Meiji Japan (1.53 per 1,000 people in 1899) but became rare as the 1898 Civil Code took hold. From the 1970s it climbed to a peak of 2.3 in 2002, then fell as fewer couples married.

source.attribution: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare of Japan, Vital Statistics (e-Stat)

questions.title: Wheat harvested per hectare in Russia
questions.hint: Think about the Green Revolution, fertilizers, and the fact that plants have biological limits.
questions.explanation: It rose to 3.2 in 2023, from 1.4 in 1995.
